title: Arithmetic exceptionality of Lattès maps
summary: Let $\mathbb{F}_q$ denote a finite field of order $q$. A rational function $r(x)\in \mathbb{Q}(x)$ is said to be arithmetically exceptional if it induces a permutation on $\mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{F}_p)$ for infinitely many primes $p$. Based on some computational results, Odabaş conjectured that for each $k\in \mathbb{N}$, the $k$-th Lattès map attached to an elliptic curve $E/\mathbb{Q}$ is arithmetically exceptional if and only if $E$ has no $k$-torsion point whose $x$-coordinate is rational.
